audits.title: Re-Audit of Benzodiazepine and Z-Drug Prescribing in Two Community Treatment Teams in the Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Trust
audits.standard: CNTW Trust Policy and BNF prescribing guidance; compliance required 90–100% of prescriptions meeting each standard
audits.setting: Two community treatment teams, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Prescribing rate 7%; documented indication 61.65%; prescriptions <4 weeks 58.2%; written advice 10.7%.

audits.intervention: Previous audit cycles (2009, 2017, 2018); interventions between cycles not described.

cycle2.result: Prescribing rate 10.8%; 100% compliance with BNF limits, avoiding diazepam 10 mg and no prescribing in pregnant/post-partum women; documented indication 80.8%; prescriptions <4 weeks 79.2%; written advice 5.8%.

audits.other_findings: Documentation of indication, duration and review plans ranged 31.5%–81.2%, verbal advice 0–16.9% and tapering plans 16.1%; 41/51 encounters were by telephone or video. Planned educational email, poster and quiz with re-audit in one year.
audits.citation: Obayi M, Hargreaves H, Ahuja N. Re-Audit of Benzodiazepine and Z-Drug Prescribing in Two Community Treatment Teams in the Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Trust. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S168-S169. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.472.

audits.title: The Management of Short-Term Insomnia for Inpatients in an Adult Acute Admissions Ward: Audit of Compliance With Local and National Guidelines
audits.standard: Local and national guidance: sleep hygiene advice before drugs; non-benzodiazepine hypnotic prescribed; one-off trial dose before regular prescription; target 100%
audits.setting: Adult Acute Admissions Ward, West of Scotland

cycle1.result: Of 8 reviewed for insomnia: 12.5% (n=1) offered sleep hygiene advice; 25% (n=2) trial dose of non-benzodiazepine hypnotic; 25% (n=3) regular hypnotic with no trial dose; 50% (n=4) alternative sedative.

audits.intervention: Planned: sleep hygiene leaflet, presentation of data to medical and nursing staff, guidelines made available on the ward; re-audit in six months.
audits.other_findings: The cohort reviewed was 21 patients, of whom 8 were reviewed for insomnia.
audits.citation: Long M, Widdowson R. The Management of Short-Term Insomnia for Inpatients in an Adult Acute Admissions Ward: Audit of Compliance With Local and National Guidelines. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S167-S168. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.443.

audits.title: Audit of Benzodiazepine and Z-Drugs Prescription in an Acute Inpatient Adult Psychiatric Unit in North Wales With the Aim of a Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: National guidelines on benzodiazepine and hypnotic treatment duration and dosage limits
audits.setting: Heddfan acute adult inpatient psychiatric unit, North Wales

cycle1.result: 38/40 prescribed PRN benzodiazepines (lorazepam 35/38, 92%); only 12/38 reviewed within a week; one had PRN stopped; half continued PRN benzodiazepines for more than 3 weeks. 20 (50%) received zopiclone, 66% (8) of these for 3 weeks or more.

audits.other_findings: 11 (27.5%) were already on regular benzodiazepines. Planned pharmacist-led weekly PRN review at ward rounds and a protocol for reducing and stopping PRN medication.
audits.citation: Anil A, Bhupal S, Soundararajan S, Turner C, Dhandapani A. Audit of Benzodiazepine and Z-Drugs Prescription in an Acute Inpatient Adult Psychiatric Unit in North Wales With the Aim of a Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S227-S228. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10571.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Use of Clonazepam in General Adult Psychiatry Patients
audits.standard: Local trust prescribing guidelines for clonazepam
audits.setting: Enhanced Team West, general adult psychiatry

cycle1.result: Appropriate indication 94%; consultant oversight 88%; unlicensed medicine form 6%; weekly review 100%; discontinuation plan before discharge 47%.

audits.intervention: Recommended: training on unlicensed medicine documentation and reinforced discharge planning.
audits.other_findings: Among those continued after discharge, 89% had documented dose-reduction attempts in the community.
audits.citation: Ahmadie N, Sturgess C, Nazari J. Clinical Audit of Use of Clonazepam in General Adult Psychiatry Patients. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S232-S232. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10581.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Discontinuation Plans on Discharge for Prescribed Hypnotics in General Adult Inpatient Services
audits.standard: Discharge summaries to include hypnotic medication review and specific discontinuation plan for the GP; target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: 0% compliance on two wards: no discharge summaries had a hypnotic medication review or discontinuation plan.

audits.intervention: Implementation of previous audit recommendations (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Across six wards, 56.25% included a medication review for hypnotics and 18.75% a specific discontinuation plan.

audits.other_findings: A 2024 re-audit on the original two wards showed 66.6% with medication review and 33.3% with a specific discontinuation plan.
audits.citation: Radwan R, Mujtaba A. Re-Audit of Discontinuation Plans on Discharge for Prescribed Hypnotics in General Adult Inpatient Services. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S270-S270. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10659.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project on Benzodiazepine Prescribing on Discharge and Compliance with Trust Guidelines
audits.standard: SPFT guidelines: 100% with date of initiation and indication recorded, consultant support for continuation, and indication, duration, dose and reducing regimen communicated to GP
audits.setting: Eastbourne Department of Psychiatry, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 12.5% regular and 15% PRN benzodiazepines on discharge; of these 80% on long-term treatment and 40% had documented indication and reducing regimen.

audits.intervention: Teaching on benzodiazepine prescribing for residents at the start of rotation.

cycle2.result: 9% regular and 0% PRN on discharge; 100% consultant supported with indication, duration and reducing regimen documented.

audits.other_findings: Re-audit covered only the male ward, limiting generalisability.
audits.citation: Lewis M, DiFrancesco D, Jullian L. Quality Improvement Project on Benzodiazepine Prescribing on Discharge and Compliance with Trust Guidelines. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S169-S170. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11418.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project on the Use of Zopiclone on Elm Ward, West Park Hospital
audits.standard: NICE TA77: zopiclone not exceeding four weeks including tapering
audits.setting: Elm Ward, West Park Hospital, Tees, Esk and Wear Valley

cycle1.result: Mean duration 7.7 weeks (median 8.3); 27% (6/22) within the ≤4-week limit.

audits.intervention: Practice changes introduced after the initial audit (not described).

cycle2.result: Mean duration 3.42 weeks, median 1.29 weeks; 83.3% (10/12) within ≤4 weeks; 30% of evaluable cases met indication-specific NICE durations.

audits.other_findings: Stop dates, indications, review plans and non-pharmacological interventions remained poorly documented.
audits.citation: Ohene O, Anakwe O. Quality Improvement Project on the Use of Zopiclone on Elm Ward, West Park Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S184-S184. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11449.

audits.title: Audit of Sleep Assessment and Management in Older Adults Across Mental Health Services: Impact of a Targeted Educational Intervention
audits.standard: NICE NG97 and NG222, NHS and RCPsych guidance on sleep assessment and management
audits.setting: Older adult inpatient wards and Community Mental Health Teams, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, Bromley

cycle1.result: Records: 23.3% detailed assessment aligned with guidance, 70% brief mention, 6.7% no documentation; pharmacological management 88.2%. Clinician survey (n=20): 45–50% routinely assessed sleep, 80% no structured tools, 10% sleep diaries, 80% unfamiliar with guidance.

audits.intervention: Targeted teaching on sleep assessment in older adults and dissemination of guidance on non-pharmacological approaches

cycle2.result: Clinician survey only: 90% reported routine sleep assessment, structured tools 81%, sleep diaries 72%, 72% familiar with guidance, 90% offering sleep hygiene advice.

audits.other_findings: Post-intervention data were self-reported by clinicians; records were reviewed only at baseline. Re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Vieira Marcque G, Khalil M, Abdelsamie A, Krishnan A, Goudaman S. Audit of Sleep Assessment and Management in Older Adults Across Mental Health Services: Impact of a Targeted Educational Intervention. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S279-S279. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11555.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of the Use, Prescribing and Review of Anxiolytics and Hypnotics Within Acute Psychiatry
audits.standard: TEWV trust policy on regular review of anxiolytics and hypnotics
audits.setting: Adult mental health male and female acute inpatient wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Inpatient prescriptions reviewed and documented: 26% (female, 100 prescriptions) and 46% (male, 35); reviewed weekly 6% (female) and 0% (male). Documented discharge plan for benzodiazepine/z-drug review 74% (female) and 91% (male).

audits.other_findings: Most prescriptions were reviewed only at discharge (71% female and 22% male discharge prescriptions changed). Weekly MDT reviews and training for doctors in training recommended.
audits.citation: Eremenko-Lowery J, Rahmatalla S. Clinical Audit of the Use, Prescribing and Review of Anxiolytics and Hypnotics Within Acute Psychiatry. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S291-S292. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11723.

audits.title: Audit on Insomnia Management in In-Patient Psychiatric Unit
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and local Trust policy on insomnia (non-pharmacological first, CBT-I, documented indication, review and stop dates for hypnotics)
audits.setting: Inpatient psychiatric unit, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Insomnia in 30 (66.6%); documented in 23 (76.6%); sleep hygiene in 11/30 (36.6%); CBT-I offered 0%; hypnotics offered to 26/30 (86.6%); 0% met all NICE and Trust criteria

audits.other_findings: A standardised insomnia care pathway was recommended.
audits.citation: Anandakumar B, Elsankary M, Malli A, Tebbs Z. Audit on Insomnia Management in In-Patient Psychiatric Unit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S347-S348. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11846.
